heading: Understanding Life Insurance Surrender Value
tldr: Surrender value is the amount you receive if you terminate a life insurance policy before its full term.
It is typically available only after paying premiums for a minimum period, usually two to three years.
The amount received is almost always less than the total premiums you have paid into the policy.
Calculation involves either a Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) or a Special Surrender Value (SSV), with SSV often being higher.
Surrendering a policy can have significant financial and tax implications, often leading to a loss.
caption:
Thinking of stopping your life insurance policy early? It's important to know what happens next. When you surrender a policy, you might get some money back, but it's often less than you paid in. This article explains "surrender value" in simple terms, so you understand the financial impact and avoid surprises. Learn more by reading the full article.
